description: WaterTAP is an open-source Python library for modelling and optimising water treatment trains and their costs. Users assemble flowsheets of unit processes, attach property and reaction packages, and solve steady-state mass and energy balances with equation-oriented optimisation to run techno-economic analyses of treatment technologies; its documentation includes, for example, a flowsheet of the IWA Benchmark Simulation Model No. 2 for a full biological wastewater treatment plant with primary clarifier, activated sludge, thickener, anaerobic digester and dewatering, which can serve as a baseline for comparing alternative plant configurations. It is developed within the National Alliance for Water Innovation with support from the U.S. Department of Energy, with contacts at Lawrence Berkeley and the National Energy Technology Laboratory. It is site-independent. The code is on GitHub, released on PyPI (version 1.7.0 on 1 July 2026) under the BSD-3-Clause licence, free of charge, with online documentation, tutorials that run in the browser, and a graphical Flowsheet Processor for Windows and macOS. Caveats: models are steady-state (the BSM2 flowsheet explicitly so), so it does not simulate network hydraulics or dynamic plant control, and it needs an optimisation solver. Simulation uses: design optimisation and capacity planning of drinking water and wastewater treatment plants. Related: the IWA Benchmark Simulation Models (model-iwa-benchmark-simulation-models).
